**Richard Wayne Van Dyke** (born December 13, 1925) is an American actor, comedian, singer, dancer and writer. [His work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke_on_screen_and_stage "Dick Van Dyke on screen and stage") spans screen and stage, and [his awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Dick_Van_Dyke "List of awards and nominations received by Dick Van Dyke") include six [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards"), a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), and a [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award "Tony Award"). He was inducted into the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") in 1993, and then the [Television Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Hall_of_Fame "Television Hall of Fame") in 1995. He was recognized as a [Disney Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Legend "Disney Legend") in 1998. He has been honored with the [Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Life_Achievement_Award "Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award") in 2013, and the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 2020.

Van Dyke began his career as an entertainer on radio, television and in nightclubs. He made his [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") debut in the musical [revue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revue "Revue")_The Girls Against the Boys_ (1959). The following year he starred as Albert F. Peterson in the original production of _[Bye Bye Birdie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye\_Bye\_Birdie "Bye Bye Birdie")_ (1960), a role which earned him the [Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actor_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical"). He returned to Broadway playing Harold Hill in a revival of _[The Music Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Music\_Man "The Music Man")_ (1980).

On television, Van Dyke became a household name in the United States and Canada portraying Rob Petrie in the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") sitcom _[The Dick Van Dyke Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dick\_Van\_Dyke\_Show "The Dick Van Dyke Show")_ (1961–1966), which also earned him three [Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lead_Actor_in_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series"). He guest-starred on shows such as _[Columbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbo "Columbo")_ (1974) and _[The Carol Burnett Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Carol\_Burnett\_Show "The Carol Burnett Show")_ (1977), and starred in _[The New Dick Van Dyke Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Dick\_Van\_Dyke\_Show "The New Dick Van Dyke Show")_ (1971–1974), _[Diagnosis: Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis:\_Murder "Diagnosis: Murder")_ (1993–2001), and _[Murder 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder\_101\_(film\_series) "Murder 101 (film series)")_ (2006–2008).

Van Dyke is also known for his role as Bert, the [cockney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockney "Cockney")[jack-of-all-trades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_of_all_trades "Jack of all trades") ([one-man band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-man_band "One-man band"), [screever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_painting "Street painting"), [chimney sweep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimney_sweep "Chimney sweep"), and kite seller) in the [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures") movie musical _[Mary Poppins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary\_Poppins\_(film) "Mary Poppins (film)")_ (1964), for which he was nominated for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). He starred in the movie musicals _[Bye Bye Birdie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye\_Bye\_Birdie\_(1963\_film) "Bye Bye Birdie (1963 film)")_ (1963) and _[Chitty Chitty Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitty\_Chitty\_Bang\_Bang "Chitty Chitty Bang Bang")_ (1968), as well as the comedy-drama _[The Comic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Comic "The Comic")_ (1969). In his later years, Van Dyke has taken supporting roles in films such as _[Dick Tracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick\_Tracy\_(1990\_film) "Dick Tracy (1990 film)")_ (1990), _[Curious George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curious\_George\_(film) "Curious George (film)")_ (2006), _[Night at the Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night\_at\_the\_Museum "Night at the Museum")_ (2006), [its 2014 sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_at_the_Museum:_Secret_of_the_Tomb "Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb"), and _[Mary Poppins Returns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary\_Poppins\_Returns "Mary Poppins Returns")_ (2018).

## Early life and education

Richard Wayne Van Dyke was born on December 13, 1925, in [West Plains, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Plains,_Missouri "West Plains, Missouri"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-museumbroadcast-1) to Hazel Victoria ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")McCord), a [stenographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stenographer "Stenographer"), and Loren Wayne "Cookie" Van Dyke, a salesman.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-2) He grew up in [Danville, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danville,_Illinois "Danville, Illinois"). He is the older brother of actor [Jerry Van Dyke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Van_Dyke "Jerry Van Dyke"), who appeared as his brother in _The Dick Van Dyke Show_. [Van Dyke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Dyke "Van Dyke") is a [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people "Dutch people") surname, although he also has English, Irish, and Scottish ancestry.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-waitwait-3) His family line traces back to _[Mayflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayflower "Mayflower")_ passenger [John Alden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Alden "John Alden").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-4)

Van Dyke attended [Danville High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danville_High_School_(Illinois) "Danville High School (Illinois)") in 1944, where he participated in the _[a cappella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_cappella "A cappella")_ choir and drama club.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-McGee2004-5) He performed in the drama program with [Bobby Short](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Short "Bobby Short") and [Donald O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_O'Connor "Donald O'Connor"), and his involvement convinced him to become a professional entertainer, although he also considered a career in the ministry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-memoirluckylife-6)

Van Dyke left high school during his senior year to join the [United States Army Air Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces "United States Army Air Forces") for pilot training during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-WP-Showman-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-Grunge-WWII-8) He was repeatedly rejected for being underweight before being accepted after eating numerous bananas and drinking a large amount of water prior to the weigh-in. He then began pilot training before transferring to the [Special Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Services_(entertainment) "Special Services (entertainment)"). He built and painted sets and performed for military personnel at [Majors Army Airfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majors_Airport "Majors Airport") in [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas") and then served as a radio announcer.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-10) He was discharged in 1946.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-11) Van Dyke received his high school diploma in 2004.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-12)

## Career

### 1947–1959: Early work and Broadway debut

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Dick_Van_Dyke_1959.jpg/250px-Dick_Van_Dyke_1959.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dick_Van_Dyke_1959.jpg)

Van Dyke in a 1959 publicity photo

During the late 1940s, Van Dyke was a [radio DJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_DJ "Radio DJ") on [WDAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WDAN "WDAN") in [Danville, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danville,_Illinois "Danville, Illinois").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-13) In 1947, Van Dyke was persuaded by [pantomime performer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mime_artist "Mime artist") Phil Erickson[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-14) to form a comedy duo called "Eric and Van—the Merry Mutes."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-15) The team toured the [West Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_of_the_United_States "West Coast of the United States") nightclub circuit, performing a mime act and [lip synching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lip_sync "Lip sync") to [78 rpm records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonograph_record "Phonograph record"). They moved to [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta"), Georgia, in the early 1950s and performed on a local television show featuring original skits and music called _The Merry Mutes_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-16) The Monday-Friday show debuted on [WSB-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSB-TV "WSB-TV") on April 26, 1954.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-17)

In Atlanta, Van Dyke also worked as a morning disc jockey and radio talk show host. In 1953, he began hosting a daily children's show on a local Atlanta television station.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-18)

Van Dyke worked in televion with [WDSU-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WDSU "WDSU")[New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") Channel 6 ([NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")), first as a single comedian and later as [emcee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emcee "Emcee") of a comedy program.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-20) Van Dyke's first network TV appearance was with [Dennis James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_James "Dennis James") on James' _[Chance of a Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chance\_of\_a\_Lifetime\_(TV\_series) "Chance of a Lifetime (TV series)")_ in 1954. He later appeared in two episodes of _[The Phil Silvers Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phil\_Silvers\_Show "The Phil Silvers Show")_ during its 1957–58 season. He also appeared early in his career on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _The Pat Boone Chevy Showroom_ and [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Broadcasting_Company "National Broadcasting Company")'s _The Polly Bergen Show_. During this time a friend from the Army was working as an executive for CBS television and recommended Van Dyke to that network. Out of this came a seven-year contract with the network.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-King2010-21) During an interview on [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR")'s _[Wait Wait... Don't Tell Me!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wait\_Wait...\_Don't\_Tell\_Me! "Wait Wait... Don't Tell Me!")_ program, Van Dyke said he was the anchorman for the [CBS Morning Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Early_Show "The Early Show") during this period with [Walter Cronkite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Cronkite "Walter Cronkite") as his newsman.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-waitwait-3)

In November 1959, Van Dyke made his [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") debut in _The Girls Against the Boys_ which ran at the [Alvin Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvin_Theatre "Alvin Theatre"). The production was a revue in two acts and featured performances from Van Dyke, [Shelley Berman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelley_Berman "Shelley Berman"), [Bert Lahr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bert_Lahr "Bert Lahr"), [Nancy Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Walker "Nancy Walker") among many others. The production ran on Broadway for 16 performances from November 2 to 14, 1959.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-22)

### 1960–1968: Career stardom

#### _Bye Bye Birdie_ (1960–1963)

Van Dyke played the lead role of Albert Peterson in _Bye Bye Birdie_, which ran from April 14, 1960, to October 7, 1961. Van Dyke starred alongside [Chita Rivera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chita_Rivera "Chita Rivera"), Barbara Doherty, and [Paul Lynde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Lynde "Paul Lynde"). The production received mixed reviews from critics, such as from [Brooks Atkinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooks_Atkinson "Brooks Atkinson") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, who praised Van Dyke as "likable" but opined, "As a production it's neither fish fowl nor good musical comedy. It needs work." Despite this, the musical won four Tony awards, including for Van Dyke, who won the Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical in 1961.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-23)

Van Dyke began his film career by playing the role of Albert J. Peterson in the film version of _[Bye Bye Birdie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye\_Bye\_Birdie\_(1963\_film) "Bye Bye Birdie (1963 film)")_ (1963). Despite his unhappiness with the adaptation—its focus differed from the stage version in that the story now centered on a previously supporting character[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-24)—the film was a success. The film starred [Ann-Margret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann-Margret "Ann-Margret"), [Janet Leigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Leigh "Janet Leigh"), and [Maureen Stapleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maureen_Stapleton "Maureen Stapleton") with Van Dyke and Lynde reprising their roles. _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ wrote of Van Dyke's performance, "Van Dyke displays a showbiz knowhow far more extensive than his television outings communicate".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-25)

#### _The Dick Van Dyke Show_ (1961–1966)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Dick_Van_Dyke_in_1964.JPG/250px-Dick_Van_Dyke_in_1964.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dick_Van_Dyke_in_1964.JPG)

Van Dyke in 1964

From 1961 to 1966, Van Dyke starred in the CBS sitcom _[The Dick Van Dyke Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dick\_Van\_Dyke\_Show "The Dick Van Dyke Show")_, in which he portrayed a comedy writer named [Rob Petrie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Petrie "Rob Petrie"). Carl Reiner conceived the program and cast himself as the lead in the pilot, but CBS insisted on recasting, and Reiner chose Van Dyke to replace him in the role.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-King2010-21) Complementing Van Dyke was a veteran cast of comic actors including [Rose Marie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Marie "Rose Marie"), [Morey Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morey_Amsterdam "Morey Amsterdam"), [Jerry Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Paris "Jerry Paris"), [Ann Morgan Guilbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Morgan_Guilbert "Ann Morgan Guilbert"), [Richard Deacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Deacon_(actor) "Richard Deacon (actor)"), and [Carl Reiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Reiner "Carl Reiner") (as Alan Brady), as well as 24-year-old [Mary Tyler Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Tyler_Moore "Mary Tyler Moore"), who played Rob's wife [Laura Petrie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Petrie "Laura Petrie"). Van Dyke won three Emmy Awards as [Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lead_Actor_in_a_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series"), and the series received four [Emmy Awards as Outstanding Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Comedy_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-museum-26)

_The Dick Van Dyke Show_ received positive reviews from its start, with _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ praising Van Dyke's comedic performance writing, "Sure to catch on as a new personality is Dick Van Dyke who, though he can play it straight when need be, proves a master of the double take, juicing up to solid laughs what would possibly be just amusing lines with his physical reactions. Yet, he doesn't over-mug. In this one, his "drunk husband" bit was a masterpiece of timing and ingenuity."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-27)

Ken Tucker of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ reviewed the series following its [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") boxset release in 2012 writing, "The Dick Van Dyke Show certainly wasn't the first sitcom featuring a lead character who presided over a TV-show-within-the-TV-show—[Jack Benny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Benny "Jack Benny")'s _[The Jack Benny Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jack\_Benny\_Program "The Jack Benny Program")_, among others, had beaten Van Dyke to that. But this was the first sitcom to meld the workplace sitcom with the domestic sitcom so seamlessly. The episodes themselves move with the same smoothness and grace that Van Dyke and Moore did, whether the Petries were clowning, dancing, or romancing".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-28)

The series had a reunion in 2004 and was aired on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") as _The Dick Van Dyke Show Revisited_ with [Ray Romano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Romano "Ray Romano") serving as host and Van Dyke, [Mary Tyler Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Tyler_Moore "Mary Tyler Moore"), [Rose Marie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Marie "Rose Marie"), Jerry Van Dyke and [Carl Reiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Reiner "Carl Reiner") returning. [Morey Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morey_Amsterdam "Morey Amsterdam") and [Richard Deacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Deacon_(actor) "Richard Deacon (actor)") appeared in archival footage, both having died.

#### _Mary Poppins_ (1964)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Mary_Poppins9.jpg/250px-Mary_Poppins9.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mary_Poppins9.jpg)

Van Dyke in _[Mary Poppins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary\_Poppins\_(film) "Mary Poppins (film)")_, 1964

In 1964, Van Dyke was cast in two roles in [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney")'s _Mary Poppins_: as Bert, a man who goes through multiple odd jobs, ultimately and memorably becoming a [chimney sweep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimney_sweep "Chimney sweep"); and as bank chairman Mr. Dawes Senior. For his scenes as the chairman, he was heavily costumed to look much older and was credited in that role as "Navckid Keyd". At the end of the credits, the letters [unscramble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anagram "Anagram") into "Dick Van Dyke", which was repeated in _Mary Poppins Returns_. In a 2003 poll by _[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire\_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")_ magazine of the worst-ever accents in film, his Cockney accent came in second (to [Sean Connery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Connery "Sean Connery")'s performance as an American in _[The Untouchables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Untouchables\_(film) "The Untouchables (film)")_, despite Connery winning an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") for that performance).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-30)

According to Van Dyke, his accent coach—veteran actor [J. Pat O'Malley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Pat_O'Malley "J. Pat O'Malley")—was Irish and "didn't do an accent any better than I did", and no one alerted him to how bad it was during the production.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-31)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-waitwait-3)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-King2010-21)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-32) Still, _Mary Poppins_ was successful on release and its appeal has endured. "[Chim Chim Cher-ee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chim_Chim_Cher-ee "Chim Chim Cher-ee")", one of the songs that Van Dyke performed in _Mary Poppins_, won the [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") for the [Sherman Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherman_Brothers "Sherman Brothers"), the film's songwriting duo. Van Dyke received a Grammy Award in 1964, along with [Julie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Andrews "Julie Andrews"), for his performance on the soundtrack to _Mary Poppins_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-33)

Many of the comedy films Van Dyke starred in throughout the 1960s were relatively unsuccessful at the box office, including _[What a Way to Go!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What\_a\_Way\_to\_Go! "What a Way to Go!")_ with [Shirley MacLaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_MacLaine "Shirley MacLaine"), _[Lt. Robin Crusoe, U.S.N.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lt.\_Robin\_Crusoe,\_U.S.N. "Lt. Robin Crusoe, U.S.N.")_, _[Fitzwilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitzwilly "Fitzwilly")_, _[The Art of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Art\_of\_Love\_(1965\_film) "The Art of Love (1965 film)")_ with [James Garner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Garner "James Garner") and [Elke Sommer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elke_Sommer "Elke Sommer"), _[Some Kind of a Nut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some\_Kind\_of\_a\_Nut "Some Kind of a Nut")_, _[Never a Dull Moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never\_a\_Dull\_Moment\_(1968\_film) "Never a Dull Moment (1968 film)")_ with [Edward G. Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_G._Robinson "Edward G. Robinson"), and _[Divorce American Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divorce\_American\_Style "Divorce American Style")_ with [Debbie Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Reynolds "Debbie Reynolds") and [Jean Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Simmons "Jean Simmons"). But he also starred as [Caractacus Potts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caractacus_Potts "Caractacus Potts") (with his native accent, at his own insistence, despite the English setting) in the successful musical version of [Ian Fleming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Fleming "Ian Fleming")'s _[Chitty Chitty Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitty\_Chitty\_Bang\_Bang "Chitty Chitty Bang Bang")_ (1968), which co-starred [Sally Ann Howes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sally_Ann_Howes "Sally Ann Howes") and featured the same songwriters (the Sherman Brothers) and choreographers ([Marc Breaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Breaux "Marc Breaux") and Dee Dee Wood) as _Mary Poppins_.

### 1969–1992: Established star

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Dick_Van_Dyke_Mary_Tyler_Moore_Dick_Van_Dyke_Show_1961.JPG/250px-Dick_Van_Dyke_Mary_Tyler_Moore_Dick_Van_Dyke_Show_1961.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dick_Van_Dyke_Mary_Tyler_Moore_Dick_Van_Dyke_Show_1961.JPG)

Van Dyke and [Mary Tyler Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Tyler_Moore "Mary Tyler Moore") from the premiere of _[The Dick Van Dyke Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dick\_Van\_Dyke\_Show "The Dick Van Dyke Show")_, 1961

In 1968, it was reported that [Albert R. Broccoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_R._Broccoli "Albert R. Broccoli") had offered Van Dyke the chance to replace [Sean Connery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Connery "Sean Connery") as [James Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bond "James Bond"). Van Dyke declined the offer, asking Broccoli: "Have you heard my British accent?".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-34) In 1969, Van Dyke appeared in the comedy-drama _[The Comic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Comic "The Comic")_, written and directed by Carl Reiner. Van Dyke portrayed a self-destructive [silent film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_film "Silent film") era comedian who struggles with [alcoholism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism "Alcoholism"), [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_depressive_disorder "Major depressive disorder"), and his own rampant ego. Reiner wrote the film especially for Van Dyke, who often spoke of his admiration for silent film era comedians such as [Charlie Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Chaplin "Charlie Chaplin") and his hero [Stan Laurel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Laurel "Stan Laurel").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-35)

Also in 1969, Van Dyke played Rev. Clayton Brooks, a small-town minister who leads his Iowa town to quit smoking for 30 days to win $25 million (equal to $219,487,296 today) from a tobacco company. The film, _[Cold Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_Turkey\_(1971\_film) "Cold Turkey (1971 film)")_, was not released until 1971. In 1970, he published _Faith, Hope and Hilarity: A Child's Eye View of Religion_ a book of humorous anecdotes based largely on his experiences as a [Sunday School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday_School "Sunday School") teacher.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-36) Van Dyke was principal in "KXIV Inc." and owned 1400 AM [KXIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSUN "KSUN") in Phoenix from 1965 to 1982.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-38)

From 1971 to 1974, Van Dyke starred in an unrelated sitcom called _[The New Dick Van Dyke Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Dick\_Van\_Dyke\_Show "The New Dick Van Dyke Show")_ in which he portrayed a local television talk show host. Although the series was developed by Carl Reiner and starred [Hope Lange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Lange "Hope Lange") as his wife, and he received a [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nomination for his performance, the show was less successful than its predecessor,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-39) and Van Dyke pulled the plug on the show after just three seasons.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-40)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Tim_Conway_Carol_Burnett_Dick_Van_Dyke_Carol_Burnett_Show_1977.JPG/250px-Tim_Conway_Carol_Burnett_Dick_Van_Dyke_Carol_Burnett_Show_1977.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tim_Conway_Carol_Burnett_Dick_Van_Dyke_Carol_Burnett_Show_1977.JPG)

[Tim Conway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Conway "Tim Conway"), [Carol Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Burnett "Carol Burnett") and Van Dyke, 1977

In 1973, Van Dyke voiced his animated likeness for the October 27, 1973, installment of [Hanna-Barbera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanna-Barbera "Hanna-Barbera")'s _[The New Scooby-Doo Movies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Scooby-Doo\_Movies "The New Scooby-Doo Movies")_, "Scooby-Doo Meets Dick Van Dyke", the series' final first-run episode. In 1974, he received an Emmy Award nomination for his role as an alcoholic businessman in the television movie _[The Morning After](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Morning\_After\_(1974\_film) "The Morning After (1974 film)")_ (1974). Van Dyke revealed after its release that he had recently overcome a real-life [drinking problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism "Alcoholism"); he admitted he had been an alcoholic for 25 years.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-41) That same year he guest-starred as a murderous photographer on an episode of _[Columbo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbo "Columbo")_, _[Negative Reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List\_of\_Columbo\_episodes#Season\_4 "List of Columbo episodes")_.

In 1976, Van Dyke returned to comedy with the [sketch comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sketch_comedy "Sketch comedy") show _[Van Dyke and Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van\_Dyke\_and\_Company "Van Dyke and Company"),_ on which [Andy Kaufman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Kaufman "Andy Kaufman") made his prime time debut.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-43) Despite being canceled after three months, the show won an [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award") for Outstanding Comedy-Variety Series.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-44) After a few guest appearances on the long-running comedy-variety series _[The Carol Burnett Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Carol\_Burnett\_Show "The Carol Burnett Show")_, Van Dyke became a regular on the show, in the fall of 1977. He appeared in half of the episodes of the final season.

In 1980, Van Dyke appeared in the title role in a United States tour and [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre")[revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_(theatre) "Revival (theatre)") of _[The Music Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Music\_Man "The Music Man")_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-45)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Dick_Van_Dyke_2_crop.jpg/250px-Dick_Van_Dyke_2_crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dick_Van_Dyke_2_crop.jpg)

Van Dyke in 1988

For the next decade he appeared mostly in TV movies, including a made-for-cable remake of _The Country Girl_ (1982) with [Faye Dunaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faye_Dunaway "Faye Dunaway"). One atypical role was as a murdering judge on the second episode of the TV series _[Matlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matlock\_(1986\_TV\_series) "Matlock (1986 TV series)")_ in 1986 starring [Andy Griffith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Griffith "Andy Griffith"). In 1987, he guest-starred in an episode of _[Airwolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airwolf "Airwolf")_, with his son [Barry Van Dyke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Van_Dyke "Barry Van Dyke"), who was the lead star of the show's fourth and final season on [USA Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Network "USA Network"). In 1989, he guest-starred on the NBC comedy series _[The Golden Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Golden\_Girls "The Golden Girls")_ portraying a lover of [Beatrice Arthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bea_Arthur "Bea Arthur")'s character. This role earned him his first Emmy Award nomination since 1977.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-46)

On _[Larry King Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry\_King\_Live "Larry King Live")_, Van Dyke mentioned that he turned down the lead role in _[The Omen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Omen "The Omen")_ which was played by Gregory Peck. He also mentioned that his dream role would have been the [Scarecrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarecrow_(Oz) "Scarecrow (Oz)") in _[The Wizard of Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wizard\_of\_Oz "The Wizard of Oz")_. Twenty-one years later in 1990, Van Dyke, whose usual role had been the amiable hero, took a small but villainous turn as crooked DA Fletcher in [Warren Beatty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Beatty "Warren Beatty")'s film _[Dick Tracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick\_Tracy\_(1990\_film) "Dick Tracy (1990 film)")_.

### 1993–2001: _Diagnosis Murder_

Van Dyke's film work affected his TV career: the reviews he received for his role as DA Fletcher in _Dick Tracy_ led him to star as the character [Dr. Mark Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Sloan_(Diagnosis:_Murder) "Mark Sloan (Diagnosis: Murder)") first in an episode of _[Jake and the Fatman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake\_and\_the\_Fatman "Jake and the Fatman")_, then in a series of TV movies on CBS that became the foundation for his popular television drama _[Diagnosis: Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis:\_Murder "Diagnosis: Murder")._ The series ran from 1993 to 2001 with son [Barry Van Dyke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Van_Dyke "Barry Van Dyke") co-starring in the role of Dr. Sloan's son [Lieutenant Detective Steve Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Detective_Steve_Sloan "Lieutenant Detective Steve Sloan"). Also starring on the same show was daytime soap actress [Victoria Rowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Rowell "Victoria Rowell") as Dr. Sloan's pathologist/medical partner, [Dr. Amanda Bentley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Amanda_Bentley "Dr. Amanda Bentley"), and [Charlie Schlatter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Schlatter "Charlie Schlatter") in the role of Dr. Sloan's student, [Dr. Jesse Travis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Jesse_Travis "Dr. Jesse Travis").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-47)

Van Dyke became a [computer animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_animation "Computer animation") enthusiast after purchasing an [Amiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amiga "Amiga") in 1991. He is credited with the creation of 3D-rendered effects used on the _Diagnosis: Murder_ episode "Down and Dirty Dead" and _[The Dick Van Dyke Show Revisited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dick\_Van\_Dyke\_Show\_Revisited "The Dick Van Dyke Show Revisited")_. Van Dyke has displayed his [computer-generated imagery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") work at [SIGGRAPH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIGGRAPH "SIGGRAPH"), and continues to work with [LightWave 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LightWave_3D "LightWave 3D").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-hafner20000622-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-51)

As an [a cappella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_cappella "A cappella") enthusiast, Van Dyke has sung in a group called "[Dick Van Dyke and The Vantastix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke_and_The_Vantastix "Dick Van Dyke and The Vantastix")" since September 2000. The [quartet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartet "Quartet") has performed several times in Los Angeles as well as on _[Larry King Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry\_King\_Live "Larry King Live")_, The First Annual [TV Land Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TV_Land_Award "TV Land Award"), and sang the [national anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_anthem "National anthem") at three [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") games including a nationally televised [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") performance on NBC. Van Dyke was made an honorary member of the [Barbershop Harmony Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbershop_Harmony_Society "Barbershop Harmony Society") in 1999.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-52)

### 2002–2025: Later career and television resurgence

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Barack_Obama_adjusting_Dick_Van_Dyke%27s_tie.jpg/250px-Barack_Obama_adjusting_Dick_Van_Dyke%27s_tie.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barack_Obama_adjusting_Dick_Van_Dyke's_tie.jpg)

President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") with Van Dyke, 2010

Van Dyke continued to find television work after _Diagnosis: Murder_, including a dramatically and critically successful performance of _[The Gin Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Gin\_Game "The Gin Game")_, produced for television in 2003 that reunited him with [Mary Tyler Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Tyler_Moore "Mary Tyler Moore"). In 2003, he portrayed Doctor Doug Townshend on _[Scrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scrubs\_(2001\_TV\_series) "Scrubs (2001 TV series)")_. A 2004 special of _The Dick Van Dyke Show_ titled _The Dick Van Dyke Show Revisited_ was heavily promoted as the first new episode of the classic series to be shown in 38 years. Van Dyke and his surviving cast members recreated their roles and was nominated for a Primetime Emmy.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-54)

In 2006 Van Dyke starred as college professor Dr. Jonathan Maxwell for a series of _[Murder 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder\_101\_(TV\_film\_series) "Murder 101 (TV film series)")_ mystery films on the [Hallmark Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallmark_Channel "Hallmark Channel"), once again with son Barry as his co-star. Van Dyke returned to motion pictures in 2006 with _[Curious George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curious\_George\_(film) "Curious George (film)")_ as Mr. Bloomsberry and villain Cecil Fredericks in the [Ben Stiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Stiller "Ben Stiller") film _[Night at the Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night\_at\_the\_Museum "Night at the Museum")_.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-55) He reprised the role in a cameo for the sequel, _[Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night\_at\_the\_Museum:\_Battle\_of\_the\_Smithsonian "Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian")_ (2009), but it was cut from the film. It can be found in the special features on the DVD release. He also played the character again in the third film, _[Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night\_at\_the\_Museum:\_Secret\_of\_the\_Tomb "Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb")_ (2014).

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Dick_Van_Dyke_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg/250px-Dick_Van_Dyke_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dick_Van_Dyke_by_Gage_Skidmore_2.jpg)

Van Dyke in 2017

In 2010, Van Dyke appeared on a children's album titled _Rhythm Train,_ with [Red Hot Chili Peppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hot_Chili_Peppers "Red Hot Chili Peppers") drummer [Chad Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Smith "Chad Smith") and singer Leslie Bixler. Van Dyke [raps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping "Rapping") on one of the album's tracks.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-56) In 2017, Van Dyke released his first solo album since 1963's _Songs I Like_. The album, _Step (Back) In Time_, was produced by Bill Bixler (who also played sax), with arrangements by Dave Enos (who also played bass) and features noted musicians John Ferraro (drums), [Tony Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Guerrero "Tony Guerrero") (trumpet & vocal duet), Mark LeBrun (piano), Charley Pollard (trombone) and Leslie Bixler (vocals).

_Step (Back) In Time_ was released by BixMix Records and showcases Van Dyke in a jazz and big band setting on classic songs from the 1920s, 1930s and 1940s. Van Dyke recorded a duet single for Christmas 2017 with actress [Jane Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Lynch "Jane Lynch"). The song, "We're Going Caroling", was written and produced by [Tony Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Guerrero "Tony Guerrero") for Lynch's KitschTone Records label as a digital-only release.

In 2018, Van Dyke portrayed Mr. Dawes Jr. in _[Mary Poppins Returns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary\_Poppins\_Returns "Mary Poppins Returns")_. He had previously portrayed both Bert and Mr. Dawes Sr. (Mr. Dawes, Jr.'s late father), in the original film.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-hollywoodreporter-57) For the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") television series, _[WandaVision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WandaVision "WandaVision")_, Van Dyke was consulted by the producers on how to emulate _The Dick Van Dyke Show_.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-58)

In 2023, Van Dyke competed in [season nine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Masked_Singer_(American_TV_series)_season_9 "The Masked Singer (American TV series) season 9") of _[The Masked Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Masked\_Singer\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Masked Singer (American TV series)")_ as "Gnome" and was the first to be eliminated. The episode had been promoted as "the most legendary, decorated and beloved unmasking in history". After Van Dyke revealed his identity, he received a lengthy standing ovation from the audience and judges. Before departing the stage, Van Dyke sang as an encore of his part in the song "[Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious "Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious")" from _Mary Poppins_, in which he starred. At age 97, Van Dyke became the oldest person ever to compete on the series.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-60) In April of the same year, it was announced Van Dyke would guest-appear on _[Days of Our Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Days\_of\_Our\_Lives "Days of Our Lives")_ for several episodes.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-61) On December 21, 2023, he was honored with a CBS special, _Dick Van Dyke: 98 Years of Magic_, celebrating his 98th birthday.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-62)

On December 13, 2024, in celebration of his 99th birthday, Van Dyke starred in the music video for the [Coldplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coldplay "Coldplay") song "[All My Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_My_Love_(Coldplay_song) "All My Love (Coldplay song)")". He produced the video with his wife, actress Arlene Silver.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-63)

### 2025–present: Centenarity and later

In December 2025, two documentaries about Van Dyke were released in honor of his 100th birthday: _Starring Dick Van Dyke_, which aired as part of the _[American Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Masters "American Masters")_ series on [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS") on December 12, 2025, and _Dick Van Dyke: 100th Celebration_, which was released in theaters from December 13 to 14, 2025.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-65)

## Influences

Van Dyke has often cited [Stan Laurel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Laurel "Stan Laurel"), [Buster Keaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buster_Keaton "Buster Keaton"), and [Carl Reiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Reiner "Carl Reiner") as his comedy influences and idols.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-67) Van Dyke stated on _[Conan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan\_(talk\_show) "Conan (talk show)")_ that he called Laurel and admitted to him that he had stolen from him over the years, and Laurel replied, "Yes, I know".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-68) Entertainers who have cited Van Dyke as an influence include [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin"), [Chevy Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevy_Chase "Chevy Chase"), [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien"), [Jim Carrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Carrey "Jim Carrey"), and [Bryan Cranston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Cranston "Bryan Cranston").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-69)

## Personal life

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Dick_Van_Dyke%27s_star_on_the_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.jpg/250px-Dick_Van_Dyke%27s_star_on_the_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dick_Van_Dyke's_star_on_the_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.jpg)

Van Dyke's star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame")

On February 12, 1948, while appearing at the Chapman Park Hotel on [Wilshire Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilshire_Boulevard "Wilshire Boulevard") in Los Angeles, Van Dyke and the former Margerie Willett were married on the radio show _Bride and Groom_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-King2010-21) They had four children: Christian, [Barry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Van_Dyke "Barry Van Dyke"), Stacy and Carrie Beth.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-usatoday-42711-70) They divorced in 1984 after a long separation.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-usatoday-42711-70)

In 1976, Van Dyke began his relationship with longtime companion [Michelle Triola Marvin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Triola_Marvin "Michelle Triola Marvin"). They reportedly lived together for more than 30 years, until her death in 2009.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-:0-73) Their affair, which left Van Dyke "writhing in guilt", contributed to the breakup of Van Dyke and Willett's marriage.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-:0-73)

On February 29, 2012, at the age of 86, Van Dyke married make-up artist Arlene Silver, 46 years his junior. The couple had met six years earlier at the [SAG awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG_awards "SAG awards").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-arlene-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-:0-73) While reporting on his 100th birthday on December 13, 2025, _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_ journalist Liz McNeil stated that Van Dyke and Silver have been together "for nearly 20 years."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-peopleexlcusive100thbirthday-75) In an exclusive interview with _People_, Silver admitted that she "didn't know a lot about him" prior to meeting him in 2006, and learned more about him through his fans on [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-peopleexlcusive100thbirthday-75) She later would "connect him with his fans" on social media, which, according to Silver, Van Dyke "never really did before."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-peopleexlcusive100thbirthday-75)

Van Dyke included his children and grandchildren in his TV shows. In addition to his son Barry Van Dyke, grandsons [Shane Van Dyke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Van_Dyke "Shane Van Dyke") and Carey Van Dyke, and other Van Dyke grandchildren and relatives also appeared in episodes of _[Diagnosis: Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis:\_Murder "Diagnosis: Murder")_. Van Dyke has seven grandchildren. His son Christian was [district attorney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_attorney "District attorney") for [Marion County, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_County,_Oregon "Marion County, Oregon"), in the 1980s[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-Altus-Chris-76) and prosecuted the [I-5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_5_in_Oregon "Interstate 5 in Oregon") Killer, [Randall Woodfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randall_Woodfield "Randall Woodfield"). In 1987, Van Dyke's granddaughter, Jessica Van Dyke, died from [Reye syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reye_syndrome "Reye syndrome"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-77) which led him to do a series of [public service announcements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_service_announcements "Public service announcements") to raise public awareness of the danger of aspirin to children.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-ReyesPSA-78)

Throughout his acting career Van Dyke continued to teach Sunday school in the Presbyterian Church where he was an elder, and he continued to read such theologians as [Martin Buber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Buber "Martin Buber"), [Paul Tillich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tillich "Paul Tillich"), and [Dietrich Bonhoeffer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietrich_Bonhoeffer "Dietrich Bonhoeffer").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-memoirluckylife-6)

On August 19, 2013, the 87-year-old Van Dyke was rescued from his [Jaguar XJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaguar_XJ "Jaguar XJ") by a passerby after the car had caught fire on the [Ventura Freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_101_in_California "U.S. Route 101 in California") in [Calabasas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabasas,_California "Calabasas, California"), [Los Angeles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County "Los Angeles County"). He was not injured in the fire, although the car burned down to its frame.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-79)

Van Dyke endorsed [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders") in the [2016 Democratic Party presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "2016 Democratic Party presidential primaries"). In July 2016, while campaigning for Sanders, Van Dyke said of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), "I haven't been this scared since the [Cuban Missile Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis "Cuban Missile Crisis"). I think the human race is hanging in a delicate balance right now, and I'm just so afraid he will put us in a war. He scares me."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-80) Van Dyke again endorsed and campaigned for Sanders in the [2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-81) Van Dyke endorsed [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") for president in the [2024 U.S. presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-83)

In December 2024, during [that season's wildfires in California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_California_wildfires "2024 California wildfires"), Van Dyke had to evacuate from his home in Malibu. He said, "I was trying to crawl to [my] car. I had exhausted myself. I couldn't get up. Three neighbors came and carried me out."[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-84) His home survived the wildfires.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-85) Soon afterward, Van Dyke evacuated his home again due to the [January 2025 Palisades Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palisades_Fire "Palisades Fire").

On December 13, 2025, Van Dyke [turned 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centenarian "Centenarian").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-86)

### Health

> No one is genetically miserable. No matter our current circumstances, we all have the capacity for a joyful life. I've made it to 99 in no small part because I have stubbornly refused to give into[_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_] the bad stuff in life: failures and defeats, personal losses, loneliness and bitterness, the physical and emotional pains of ageing. For the vast majority of my years, I have been in what I can only describe as a full-on bear hug with the experience of living. Being alive has been doing life—not like a job but rather like a giant playground.

—Van Dyke article in _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_, November 2025, on his health and outlook on life[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-87)

Van Dyke is [sober](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobriety#Recovery_support_programs "Sobriety"). In 1972, after struggling with alcoholism for years, he checked into a hospital for three weeks to be treated for his addiction.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-:0-73)

Van Dyke was a [heavy smoker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chain_smoking "Chain smoking") for most of his adult life. In a January 2013 interview with the London _[Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_, he said he had been using [Nicorette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicorette "Nicorette") gum for the past decade.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-41)

In April 2013, Van Dyke revealed that for seven years he had been experiencing symptoms of a neurological disorder, in which he felt a pounding in his head whenever he lay down. Despite his undergoing tests, no diagnosis had been made. He had to cancel scheduled appearances owing to fatigue from lack of sleep because of the medical condition. In May 2013, Van Dyke tweeted that it seemed his titanium [dental implants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dental_implant "Dental implant") might have been responsible.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-88)

In June 2025, Van Dyke was scheduled to attend a comedy event in Malibu, but had to cancel his appearance due to an undisclosed illness.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-89)

In an interview in November 2025, Van Dyke attributed his long lifespan to his positive outlook and the fact that he never gets angry.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-91)

## Acting credits and accolades

Main articles: [Dick Van Dyke on screen and stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke_on_screen_and_stage "Dick Van Dyke on screen and stage") and [List of awards and nominations received by Dick Van Dyke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Dick_Van_Dyke "List of awards and nominations received by Dick Van Dyke")

Van Dyke has received various awards, including a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), six [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards"), and a [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award "Tony Award"). In 1961 he won the [Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actor_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical") for his performance in _[Bye Bye Birdie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye\_Bye\_Birdie "Bye Bye Birdie")_. In 1964 he won a [Grammy Award for Best Children's Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Children's_Album "Grammy Award for Best Children's Album") for _Mary Poppins_. Nominated for 10 [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards"), Van Dyke received four awards for his work on _The Dick Van Dyke Show_ and _Van Dyke and Company_.

In 1998, Van Dyke was honored by the [Walt Disney Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Company "Walt Disney Company") with their [Disney Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Legends "Disney Legends") award.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-95) He became the oldest living Disney Legend following the death of [Glynis Johns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glynis_Johns "Glynis Johns") in 2024.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-96) In 2013, Van Dyke received the [Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Life_Achievement_Award "Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award").

In 2021, he was honored with the [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors"), where he was given tribute by [Julie Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Andrews "Julie Andrews"), [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin"), [Chita Rivera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chita_Rivera "Chita Rivera"), [Bryan Cranston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Cranston "Bryan Cranston"), and [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda"). [Laura Osnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Osnes "Laura Osnes") sang "[Jolly Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolly_Holiday "Jolly Holiday")", and [Derek Hough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Hough "Derek Hough") performed "[Step in Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step_in_Time "Step in Time")" both from _Mary Poppins_ (1964). Together Hough and Osnes performed "[Put on a Happy Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Put_On_a_Happy_Face_(song) "Put On a Happy Face (song)")" from _[Bye Bye Birdie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye\_Bye\_Birdie\_(musical) "Bye Bye Birdie (musical)")_. [Aaron Tveit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Tveit "Aaron Tveit") sang "Chitty Chitty Bang Bang" with [Pentatonix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentatonix "Pentatonix").

In 2024, at the age of 98, Van Dyke received the award for [Outstanding Guest Performer in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Performer_in_a_Drama_Series "Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Performer in a Drama Series") at the [51st Daytime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_Daytime_Emmy_Awards "51st Daytime Emmy Awards") for his performance on _[Days of Our Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Days\_of\_Our\_Lives "Days of Our Lives")_, becoming the oldest person to be nominated for and to win a Daytime Emmy.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Van_Dyke#cite_note-97)

# E.H. Shepard

#### Born: December 1, 1879 | Died: March 24, 1976

![Image 3: E.H. Shepard](https://www.illustrationhistory.org/images/made/images/uploads/shepard_portrait2_580_385_c1.jpg)
## Biography

**Ernest Howard Shepard** was born on December 1, 1879 in London to Henry and Jessie Shepard. Ernest’s father, Henry, was an architect from a highly respected family, and his mother was the daughter of distinguished watercolorist, William Lee. Creativity being prominent on both sides of Ernest’s family, it was unsurprising that his father wanted him to become an artist. Though his early years of childhood were happy, his life changed at ten years old when his mother died. He and his two siblings moved in with their aunts until Henry Shepard could save enough money to buy a house for them all in Hammersmith. Once settled in their new home, Ernest attended school at St. Paul’s where his uncle was headmaster. It was clear to his teachers from a young age that Ernest would excel at art, so he was enrolled in an advanced drawing class. Like **Gordon Browne**, Ernest took additional art classes on Saturdays at Heatherley’s art school in London. Though Ernest envisioned a more adventurous life for himself, he pursued a career in art by winning a scholarship to the Royal Academy Schools where he continued his art studies in “irrepressibly high spirits.” Shepard’s friendly personality, fondness for practical jokes, and theatricality earned him the nickname “Giddy-Kipper,” of which the shortened version of “Kip” stuck with him for the rest of his life.**[1]** While at the Royal Academy, Shepard met his future wife, Florence Chaplin, who was also an art student three years ahead of him. Neither of them had any money, so Florence agreed to marry Ernest when they had sufficient finances to start a life together. Coincidentally, the painting Ernest had successfully submitted to the Royal Academy exhibition of 1904 had sold for £100, while Florence had just received her payment for a completed mural commission; the two felt suddenly prosperous and decided to get married. The couple moved to Shamley Green, Surrey where they painted together and raised two children,Graham (born in 1907) and Mary (born in 1909).

Though two of Shepard’s paintings had been accepted to the Royal Academy exhibition and the Paris Salon the same year he graduated art school, he still considered himself “no good” at oil painting. He didn't believe he could handle the medium properly, so he never displayed his paintings in public again. Instead, Shepard turned his full focus to illustration, which he knew he wanted to pursue professionally. He submitted ideas to _Punch_ two or three times a week until they accepted two of his drawings in 1907. Since graduating art school, Shepard worked as a book illustrator on publications such as _Tom Brown’s Schooldays_ by Thomas Hughes, _David Copperfield_ by Charles Dickens, _Henry Esmond_ by W.M. Thackeray, _Aesop’s Fables_, and _Smouldering Fires_ by Evelyn Everett-Green. In 1914, when World War I began, Shepard enlisted in the Royal Artillery and was assigned to the 105 Siege Battery where he battled at the Somme, Arras, the Third Battle of Ypres, and in Italy. At the end of his four-year service, Shepard was awarded a Military Cross and retired with the rank of Major. While he was at war, he continued to submit ideas to _Punch_ regularly, drawing and painting the countryside around him in Europe. His perseverance clearly paid off, as upon his return home from the war he was offered to join the “table” at _Punch_. A full time position at _Punch_ was Shepard’s dream since it not only offered a regular income, but would also allow him to sit where the revered **Sir John Tenniel** had once been, and work for the landmark publication that his wife’s grandfather, **Ebenezer Landells** had founded. Shepard had been so excited that he recalled “I nearly fell off my perch when I got the letter.”**[2]**

The “table” of regular staff at _Punch_ met on a weekly basis at dinners or luncheons to discuss the two political cartoons that would be in the upcoming issue. Shepard sat next to E.V. Lucas who was an important figure in the world of _belles lettres_ and also a chairman at the publishing company Methuen. Lucas was also a friend and colleague of A.A. Milne, a prominent playwright, poet, essayist, and former assistant editor at _Punch_. In 1923, Milne sent Lucas a submission of children’s verses called _When We Were Very Young_ that featured prose he had written about his three year old son, Christopher. After Lucas had received Milne’s script at Methuen, he suggested that _Punch_ should publish some of the verses before it appeared in book form. Ernest Shepard was recommended to Milne as an illustrator for the text. Shepard illustrated eleven of Milne’s verses that appeared in _Punch_ from January to June 1924. Once Milne saw the illustrations that Shepard had created, he was enthusiastic enough about his work to invite him to illustrate the entire book. _When We Were Very Young_ was released later in 1924 and sold so well in America and England that it was reprinted four times before the year’s end.

The following year in 1925, A.A. Milne purchased Cotchford Farm in Sussex as a country home for he and his family to escape London on weekends and holidays. The house was surrounded by meadows and woods that would inspire the following books about the adventures of Winnie-the-Pooh and Christopher Robin. Though the scenery of Milne’s new house in Sussex had an influence over the setting of his stories, it was his son’s nursery toys that were direct inspiration for Pooh and his friends. Christopher Milne’s teddy bear became Winnie-the-Pooh, Eeyore was a well-loved stuffed animal whose head had started to sag by the time A.A. Milne wrote his stories giving him his “gloomy disposition,” Piglet was a present from the Milnes’ neighbors, Kanga and Roo were presents from Christopher’s parents. Owl and Rabbit were the only two characters that were invented by A.A. Milne himself.

Ernest Shepard had a wooden toy horse that he had loved dearly as a child but he was forced to part with when he moved in with his aunts after his mother died. It was this attachment to a beloved toy that may have helped him understand the importance of the _Winnie-the-Pooh_ stories and the need to create illustrations that brought Christopher Robin’s toys to life. Shepard’s own son Graham had a teddy bear named Growler that he carried around with him, and it was this bear in particular that inspired Shepard’s memorable Pooh bear. In order to follow Milne’s clear instructions for the illustrations, Shepard travelled to his country house on Cotchford Farm to observe the area which inspired Milne to write about the Hundred Acre Wood. When _Winnie-the-Pooh_ was published by Methuen in 1926, it received as much praise as _When We Were Very Young_, and prompted another two books: _Now We are Six_ was published in 1927, and _House at Pooh Corner_ was released in 1928, completing the quartet of Milne’s tales of Christopher Robin. As Susan Meyer states in _A Treasury of the Greatest Children’s Book Illustrators_, the relationship between between Milne and Shepard “demonstrates the finest example of a successful collaboration between author and illustrator.”**[3]** Though the two men were not close, and harbored very different personalities, they clearly communicated in an effective way to produce a work of art that is still cherished by children all over the world.

The success of Milne’s stories was bittersweet for both author and illustrator. Though both men were happy with the fruits of their labor, neither wanted to be associated with this single collection of writing for the rest of their lives. Milne declared that it was “easier in England to make a reputation than to lose one,”**[4]** and Shepard is known to have been frustrated that his illustrations for the Winnie-the-Pooh tales overshadowed the rest of his work. For example, the publication of _When We Were Very Young_ in 1924 completely covered any recognition he should have received for his illustrations in E.V. Lucas’ _Playtime and Company_, released immediately following Milne’s work. A.A. Milne tried his best to lose the reputation of “children’s author” though Ernest Shepard continued to illustrate Pooh for the rest of his life, creating illustrations for new editions and exhibiting his original drawings to sell in galleries. Shepard had made some money from the success of the _Winnie-the-Pooh_ books, but he had accepted a flat fee instead of royalties as payment, meaning that he could use the money made from the sales of his drawings, especially after the sudden death of his wife, Florence, in 1927. Shepard made some of his best artwork after the publishing of the Pooh books and was pleased with the amount of commissions that were sent to him in the late 1920s.

By 1931, Kenneth Grahame invited Shepard to illustrate his children’s classic The Wind in the Willows. Shepard stated “I was more excited when they offered me that than Pooh.”**[5]** Though Grahame had already asked three other illustrators to work on his book, he hadn’t liked their interpretations of his famous characters calling them “puppets.” Arthur Rackham had been invited to illustrate the story but had to turn it down due to a conflicting publication. (He would later have the chance to illustrate the story as his last artwork before his death.) Before beginning his illustrations, Shepard met with Kenneth Grahame to discuss his plans for the book and take a tour of the forest and river that inspired Grahame’s stories. The second time Shepard met with Grahame was just before his death when he had the chance to show him some of his line drawings for the book. Though Grahame would never seem them published, he told Shepard “I’m glad you made them real.”**[6]** The illustrations for _The Wind in the Willows_ were Shepard’s favorite that he ever drew.

Throughout the 1930s, Shepard maintained his work ethic, illustrating fourteen books, dust jackets and frontispieces, and continuing his contributions to _Punch_. The new editor of _Punch_ in 1932, E.V. Knox, married Shepard’s daughter, Mary in 1937. Still working at the magazine now run by his son-in-law, at the start of World War II, Shepard began drawing a series of cartoons attacking Hitler and other leaders involved in the war, though this motivation for political cartoons was short-lived and ended along with the war. Shepard admitted that, though he greatly admired Tenniel, he was not adept at caricature and continued with his usual humorous cartoons. A great deal happened as Shepard aged; his son was killed at sea near the end of World War II, Ernest himself remarried at the age of sixty-five, and he was “sacked from _Punch_” by the new editor, Malcolm Muggeridge. Between 1954-55 Ernest illustrated nine books, traveled, gave lectures, and even wrote two autobiographies: _Drawn from Memory_ (1957) and _Drawn from Life_(1961). In that same span of time, he also wrote an illustrated _Ben and Brock_ and _Betsy and Joe_. Ernest continued to draw in his nineties, his last work being the color illustrations for _Winnie the Pooh_. The publisher, Methuen, had printed his drawings for the first set of books so he could paint over them in watercolor. In less than four months, Shepard painted 240 drawings for the books, an impressive feat at ninety-three years of age. Ernest Howard Shepard died three years later on March 24, 1976, the same year as Winnie the Pooh’s 50th Anniversary.
